## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by large, flattened, nearly circular cells divided into two highly symmetrical semicells by a narrow central constriction. Micrasterias rotata has five major lobes on each semicell that are repeatedly divided into smaller, often toothed branches, producing an intricate star- or wheel-like appearance. It occurs primarily in clean, acidic to slightly acidic freshwater habitats, particularly bog pools, peatlands, ponds, and shallow waters associated with aquatic vegetation. It is relatively large for a desmid and may reach several hundred micrometers across. Like many desmids, it is especially associated with low-nutrient waters and can serve as an indicator of relatively undisturbed freshwater conditions.
